utterances.text: Is it true at least by identifying these specific individual groups that you're guessing which if anything of them might have committed this? I mean, you don't have any personal knowledge of this. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN GILBERT
utterances.text: I did not witness the destruction and be able to identify the member who did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I mean, it obviously happened, right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN GILBERT
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: But you can't identify which if any of these people in these groups conducted this. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN GILBERT
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's all I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kuzmanovic. Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Just one brief point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Captain Gilbert, just a minor point for clarification. You've just been asked a question and you answered that General Cermak came and told the refugees to stay. But in your statement, you say that these refugees were afraid for their safety because no one could guarantee the safety. How could you reconcile this, please?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN GILBERT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, General Cermak during those meetings, said that they were welcome, that they were welcome to leave the camp and go home in Knin, return to their homes in Knin, where the Croatian forces would make sure that they would be safe and that the camp -- refugees in the camp hesitated and did not really wish to go back in -- in town in Knin because they were afraid for their safety. So maybe this is a -- this reconciles this, but at least -- all I can say is that what General Cermak was saying did not reassure them at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Do you know why they feared for their safety?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN GILBERT
utterances.text: If I remember well, at first, on the 4th and the 5th and a few days later, I wasn't in charge of the refugees yet but some refugees left and went in town but they came back to the camp because they were -- they were afraid. I can't really say what exactly they saw or -- or in what circumstances they might have witnessed horrible things, but they weren't prone to going back, obviously. They did not want to go back to Knin, and you know, when you've got a great number of refugees rumour spreads very fast. People talk and word to mouth goes around on what has -- what happened, so it's -- obviously no refugee wanted to go back to Knin because they feared for their safety. Maybe because of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Captain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has the re-examination caused any need to put further questions to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Gilbert, this brings your testimony to an end in this case. I wanted to thank you for coming here to The Hague and for answering all questions put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know who to address. Is your next witness available already? We have 20 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I don't believe so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I know that there was no other witness scheduled for today, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: But she is here and will be available tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: She will be available tomorrow morning. Under those circumstances, if there is no other procedural issue to be discussed at this moment --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do have one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And maybe I'm mistaken in this impression. The next witness is not protected.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No, not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: There was some confusion on my part. So I'm glad it was cleared up. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any other matter? If not, we'll adjourn and we'll resume tomorrow, the 15th of July, at 9.00 in the morning, in Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 15th day of July, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.40 p.m.,
